threads.body: [General] `RedisConnectionManagerUtil` casts to Vert.x 4.4.5's package-private `RedisConnectionManager`, so it must be defined in the library class loader. `isHelperClass()` enables helper discovery but does not force injection for isolated advice; this currently works only while the 4.0 module is also enabled and injects the class. If `vertx-redis-client-4.0` is disabled independently, these advices silently lose targets because their access errors are suppressed. Declare the injected helper in this module as well.

replies.body:
Addressed in 2ad548d1beffb80e923bac4393fc0546592911e7.

Analysis: The helper casts to a package-private Vert.x class. The 4.4.5 module uses non-inlined advice, so the agent may isolate its helpers. `isHelperClass()` makes the helper discoverable but does not force the agent to define it in the Vert.x class loader. The module must return this helper from `injectedClassNames()` instead of relying on the 4.0 module to do so.

Upsides: The 4.4.5 module now owns the injection it needs. Its advice can set configured targets even when users disable the 4.0 module independently.

Downsides: The helper class name now appears in both sibling module declarations.

threads.body: [General] The widened helper predicate now also recognizes the nested `RedisConnectionManagerUtil$CapturedTarget`, but this module still forces injection of only the outer helper. In isolated/indy mode the outer helper is defined in the Vert.x loader while that nested class remains in the instrumentation loader, which can break helper initialization or `getRedisUriTarget()` linkage. Add the nested class to this module's injected helper names too; otherwise the existing 4.0 path has the same loader failure.

threads.body: [General] In isolated/indy mode, `injectedClassNames()` injects only the outer `RedisConnectionManagerUtil` into the Vert.x class loader. The new outer class directly references `RedisConnectionManagerUtil$CapturedTarget`, but that nested class is not injected with it; it remains in the instrumentation module class loader, so initializing the injected helper or resolving `getRedisUriTarget()` can fail with `NoClassDefFoundError`/a loader mismatch. Include the nested class name in the injected helper list as well.

threads.body: [General] This 4.4.5+ module does not instrument `connectionEndpointProvider` to set `currentServerTarget`, unlike the 4.0 module. If `vertx-redis-client-4.0` is disabled independently, the provider advice below always reads `null`, so configured targets are never attached to the `RedisURI` and stable spans fall back to the selected endpoint. Add the paired enter/exit advice for this module as well.

threads.body: [General] This module advertises the same instrumentation-name set as the 4.0 module, but `build.gradle.kts` selects the two modules with `excludeInstrumentationName("vertx-redis-client-4.4.5")` and `excludeInstrumentationName("vertx-redis-client-4.0")`. Because this module does not expose the `vertx-redis-client-4.4.5` alias, the first Muzzle pass does not exclude it and the second pass excludes both modules, so the 4.4.5+ target layer is validated/selected under the wrong range. Give this module a unique `vertx-redis-client-4.4.5` alias, as the sibling Jedis core/cluster modules do.
